# Appeal of Denial — Hip Arthroscopy (CPT 29914)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-11**
**Member:** Casey Hayes
**Member ID:** W225149976
**Reference number:** POC-8E43F25837-44913
**Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Illinois
**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery - Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 (effective 2026-08-04)
Policy document: https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-314%20Hip%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

Dear Cigna Appeals Review Team,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), which was denied on 2026-08-11 for "incomplete documentation." My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking Cigna to reconsider this decision using the plan's own published criteria and the records already submitted.

## Why I believe my records meet the plan's own criteria

The plan's policy states that:

> "femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

and lists, among those criteria:

> "◦ positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation) ◦ limited passive hip internal rotation • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration AND which must include the following (unless contraindicated):"

My records show the following:

- **Diagnosis:** An MRI arthrogram of the hip on 2026-06-08 documented an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, alpha angle 68 degrees, joint space preserved, and Tonnis grade 0.
- **Symptoms and exam findings:** I have had 24 months of progressive hip pain unrelieved by rest, with sharp anterior groin pain on sitting and pivoting, and I cannot run or squat. My exam notes document positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. I believe this corresponds to the groin-dominant, provocative-maneuver findings the plan's criteria describe, but I recognize that the exact terms used in my chart ("positive provocative testing," "range of motion limited by pain") may not use the identical wording as the policy's "positive anterior impingement sign" and "limited passive hip internal rotation." I am asking that Cigna's clinical reviewer confirm whether these findings, as documented, satisfy those specific criteria, and if not, tell me exactly what additional documentation is needed.
- **Non-surgical management:** I completed 18 visits of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification over 8 weeks (2026-05-26 to 2026-07-21), as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also took NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-23 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. Taken together, my conservative treatment spanned well over three months, and it did not resolve my symptoms.

Based on this, I believe the record supports a finding of medical necessity under the plan's own FAI criteria, but the denial notice does not explain which specific piece of documentation it considers missing or incomplete. I am asking Cigna to identify precisely what is missing, or, if the existing records are sufficient, to reverse the denial.

## What I am asking for

1. Please reconsider this denial in light of the records described above and the plan's own medical necessity criteria for FAI.
2. If any specific piece of documentation is still needed to complete the medical necessity review, please tell me exactly what is missing so my surgeon's office can provide it.
3. Please send your determination in writing.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-07, and I am submitting it well within that window. I understand I can submit this appeal by logging in at my.cigna.com to find my plan's appeal form, or by calling 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my member ID card. I will use the mailing address printed on my denial letter if mailing this appeal.

Please let me know if any additional information is needed from me or from Dr. Okafor's office.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Casey Hayes
Member ID: W225149976
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date]
